status: The strict 20% observed-instruction gate passes in seven matched pairs on the pinned completed production build; frozen-page result, immediate JavaScriptCore startup. Live functional validation is recorded separately.
scope: Fresh process launch through completed 1024x768 document-only PNG at 1x, full retained-content audit and process exit. Original-origin frozen GitHub/vlang/v replay; original HTTP Date headers retained, with the explicit shared Date-only replay prefix for site16 and later; full immediate JavaScriptCore startup. Fresh private profiles and HTTP caches; retained OS filesystem/shader caches. Five-second native capture settle after Sponsor button readiness. The site14 scope also requires the complete contributor sidebar; missing optional image content invalidated earlier cohorts. No gain is attributed to either readiness correction. Observed process-tree counters are lower bounds; exited/unsampled helpers and GPU/WindowServer exclusions are disclosed in each raw record. Compare only matched current-scope controls and candidates. No credit for changing readiness, endpoints or compiler modes.

import os,sys,json,time,tempfile,threading,hashlib,subprocess,argparse,shutil,struct
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import measure_browser_instructions as m
from page_archive import Replay
from process_instruction_counts import MacCounters
from browser_bundle_lease import canonical_bundle_lease
from chatgpt_browser_instructions import vox_replay_environment
p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('--name',required=True);p.add_argument('--order',default='control,candidate,candidate,control');p.add_argument('--sample',action='store_true');p.add_argument('--diagnostic',action='store_true');a=p.parse_args()
root=Path('Build/site-opt2-20261108').resolve();out=root/a.name;out.mkdir(exist_ok=False);replay=Replay(root/'complete-archive',out/'replay');threading.Thread(target=replay.server.serve_forever,daemon=True).start()
m.VOX_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT=88;m.VOX_CHROME_HEIGHT=112
def retain_document_png(window,screenshot,width,height):
    data=window.read_bytes();assert struct.unpack('!II',data[16:24])==(width,height)
    shutil.copyfile(window,screenshot)
m.crop_document_viewport=retain_document_png
binary=Path('/Users/alex/code/vox2/Build/v/Vox.app/Contents/MacOS/Vox').resolve();lease=canonical_bundle_lease(binary.parents[2]);lease.__enter__();sha=lambda p:hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
assets={'control':root/'control-assets','candidate':root/'wakeups-diagnostic-assets','old':Path('adblock').resolve()}
pins={str(p):sha(p) for p in [binary,*binary.parent.glob('*.dylib'),binary.with_name('VoxAdblockWorker'),*[v/n for v in assets.values() for n in ['engine.js.gz','engine.snapshot.bin','engine.snapshot.json.gz']],root/'complete-archive/manifest.json',Path(__file__),*[Path('tools')/n for n in ['measure_browser_instructions.py','process_instruction_counts.py','page_archive.py','chatgpt_browser_instructions.py','run_memory_bounded.py','browser_bundle_lease.py']]]}
config=out/'audit-config.json';config.write_text(json.dumps(dict(selectors=[dict(name='rows',selector='tr.react-directory-row',limit=100,attributes=['id']),dict(name='file_links',selector='tr.react-directory-row a[href]',limit=200,attributes=['href']),dict(name='images',selector='img',limit=200,attributes=['src','alt']),dict(name='buttons',selector='button',limit=300,attributes=['aria-label','aria-disabled','data-loading','disabled']),dict(name='hydration',selector='[data-vox-deferred-hydration]',limit=10,attributes=['app-name','partial-name']),dict(name='readme',selector='article.markdown-body',limit=10,attributes=[]),dict(name='latest_commit',selector='[data-testid=latest-commit]',limit=10,attributes=[]),dict(name='commit_links',selector='tr.react-directory-row a[href*="/commit/"]',limit=200,attributes=['href']),dict(name='clock',selector='html',limit=1,attributes=['data-vox-css-aliases'])],describe_native_errors=True)))
(out/'pins.json').write_text(json.dumps(pins,indent=2));results=[];samples=[];original_popen=subprocess.Popen
try:
 for index,kind in enumerate(a.order.split(',')):
  if any(sha(Path(p))!=v for p,v in pins.items()):raise RuntimeError('Pinned input changed')
  prefix=out/f'{index}-{kind}';started=time.time();host=dict(cpu_count=os.cpu_count(),load=os.getloadavg(),started=started)
  def launch(cmd,*args,**kw):
   proc=original_popen(cmd,*args,**kw)
   if a.sample and str(cmd[0])==str(binary):
    threading.Timer(.3,lambda:samples.append(original_popen(['sample',str(proc.pid),'5','-file',str(prefix)+'.sample.txt'],stdout=(out/'sample.stdout').open('a'),stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))).start()
   return proc
  with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=out) as profile,tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=out) as cache:
   env={k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(('VOX_','LADYBIRD_','GC_','JSC_','DYLD_')) and not k.lower().endswith('_proxy')};env.update(vox_replay_environment(replay.ready['proxy'],replay.ready['ca'],True));env.update(VOX_ADBLOCK_ENGINE_ASSETS=str(assets[kind]),VOX_PROFILE_DIR=profile,VOX_TEST_WINDOW='1',VOX_CAPTURE_DOCUMENT_ONLY='1',VOX_CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR='[data-testid=sponsor-button]:not([aria-disabled="true"])',VOX_CAPTURE_AUDIT_PATH=str(prefix)+'.audit.json',VOX_CAPTURE_AUDIT_CONFIG=str(config));
   if kind=='control':env.update(VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_RASTER_INPUT_REUSE='1',VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_IMAGE_LAYOUT_BATCHING='1',VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_SVG_PATH_CACHE='1',VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_STYLESHEET_LAYOUT_REUSE='1',VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_INITIAL_STYLESHEET_DEDUP='1',VOX_DISABLE_GITHUB_ANIMATION_WAKEUP_THROTTLING='1')
   if a.diagnostic:env.update(VOX_GITHUB_RASTER_INPUT_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_STATIONARY_RASTER_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_GITHUB_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_GITHUB_SVG_PATH_CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_GITHUB_STYLESHEET_LAYOUT_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_GITHUB_INITIAL_STYLESHEET_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_GITHUB_ANIMATION_WAKEUP_DIAGNOSTICS='1',VOX_DIAGNOSTIC_LOAD_STAGES='1',VOX_DIAGNOSTIC_THREAD_LOAD_STAGES='1')
   os.environ.clear();os.environ.update(env)
   args=SimpleNamespace(binary=binary,url='https://github.com/vlang/v',width=1024,height=768,timeout=120,native_instruction_markers=a.diagnostic,settle_seconds=5,sample_interval=.005,vox_arg=['--enable-javascript','--screenshot-viewport-height','768'])
   subprocess.Popen=launch
   try:r=m.run_vox(args,prefix,MacCounters(),Path(cache))
   finally:subprocess.Popen=original_popen
  r.update(kind=kind,host_before=host,host_after=dict(load=os.getloadavg(),finished=time.time()),audit=json.loads(Path(str(prefix)+'.audit.json').read_text()));(out/f'{index}-{kind}.json').write_text(json.dumps(r,indent=2));results.append(r)
  print(json.dumps(dict(kind=kind,count=r['instructions'],title=r['audit'].get('title'),diagnostics=r['audit'].get('javascript_diagnostics'),counts=[(x['name'],x['count']) for x in r['audit'].get('selections',[])])),flush=True)
finally:
 for s in samples:s.wait()
 (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(records=results,pins=pins,identity_stable=all(sha(Path(p))==v for p,v in pins.items())),indent=2));replay.server.shutdown();replay.server.server_close();lease.__exit__(None,None,None)

from pathlib import Path
import json
root=Path('Build/site-opt2-20261108');v=json.loads((root/'site20-acceptance/verification.json').read_text());assert v['acceptance']
median=100*v['median_reduction'];conservative=100*v['conservative_reduction'];lo=min(v['controls']);hi=max(v['candidates'])
p=Path('docs/GITHUB_SITE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md');s=p.read_text();heading='# GitHub site policy, 2026-11-08\n\n';assert s.startswith(heading)
latest=f'''The requested **20% reduction is established for the frozen, full-JavaScript
startup-and-capture workload**. Seven matched control/candidate pairs show
**{median:.2f}% fewer observed instructions between medians**, with a conservative
**{conservative:.2f}% reduction** using the highest candidate and lowest control.
The app starts immediately; no interaction-triggered script loading is added.

| Statistic | Control | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median observed instructions | {v['median_control']:,} | {v['median_candidate']:,} |
| Conservative gate inputs | {lo:,} (lowest) | {hi:,} (highest) |

The integer gate passes: `5 × {hi} = {5*hi}` is at most
`4 × {lo} = {4*lo}`. This compares the combined GitHub site policies with their
rollback controls in the **same executable**, plus original versus optimized
resource assets. It does not isolate the contribution of any individual policy.
The [complete evidence](performance/github-raster-input-validation-20261108.json)
retains every observation and failed attempt, exact process counters, host load,
commands, exits, source/native input manifests and semantic/pixel audits.

The pinned completed production-build artifact is executable SHA256
`91be2b76025a47d21d22e7f40d13ebc47c81da4832515014a72c3506da579831`, receipt
`20261108-151324-a8c2bca5`: JavaScriptCore, GG adapters, one C unit and literal
V `-prod` disabled. It was checked directly in the shared publisher's staging
location under its artifact lease. This result identifies that compiled artifact;
it does not imply that an older installed bundle contains these changes.

The endpoint includes fresh process startup, native window setup, resource
loading, document-only 1024×768 PNG encoding at 1×, retained-content audit and
teardown. Each side uses a fresh private profile and HTTP cache, the same
original-origin archived responses and the same Date-only replay prefix. OS
filesystem/shader caches remain warm. Capture waits for the hydrated Sponsor
button and complete contributor sidebar, then settles for five seconds. Scripts,
timers and performance clocks execute normally. Counts are sampled process-tree
lower bounds, including charged root CPU work; missing final helper samples and
GPU/WindowServer exclusions prevent a complete-browser instruction-total claim.
The result applies to this frozen launch/capture workload, not isolated rendering,
live-site performance, scrolling FPS or a comparison with Brave.

All fourteen captures match the **unchanged original reference exactly**, with
33 directory rows, 141 file links, 53 commit links, all 39 images, latest-commit
metadata and the full README. Every browser exits normally with zero reported
native or JavaScript errors. Both independent animation-time probes agree with
`performance.now()` within their read brackets. A separate diagnostic confirms
the new cosmetic-token reuse path and cross-generation native raster reuse.
Headless startup, all 11 default screenshots, all eight SVG mutation checks and
the image/style/SVG mutation proof pass. A fresh live GitHub load also passes
with 34 rows, 51 commit links and the README, without reported errors; it is a
functional check, not a live performance comparison.

The final policy (`43af24792`) avoids repeating GitHub's cosmetic ID/class survey
after unrelated attributes, text-only edits and detached/shadow mutations. Light
DOM element membership and relevant ID/class changes still invalidate it.
Procedural filtering and live CSS matching continue. Four DOM cases, three policy
cases in enabled/rollback modes and all five existing cache regressions under
preallocation pass. ChatGPT and GitHub policy live in the `site_optimizations/`
virtual module; the historical sections below retain the path to this result.

## Initial diagnostic (historical)

'''
s=heading+latest+s[len(heading):]
s=s.replace('this latest policy remain pending.', 'this latest policy are verified by the final seven-pair cohort above.')
p.write_text(s)
p=Path('site_optimizations/README.md');s=p.read_text();s=s.replace('Removing collection code does not establish a rendering instruction reduction.\nThe GitHub 20% target remains open; see\n[the diagnostic report](../docs/GITHUB_SITE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md) before making a\nperformance claim.',f'The combined GitHub policies pass the 20% target on the frozen full-JavaScript\nlaunch/capture workload: {median:.2f}% fewer observed instructions between medians,\n{conservative:.2f}% conservatively, across seven matched pairs with exact original\npixels. See [the measured scope and evidence](../docs/GITHUB_SITE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md);\nthis does not establish live-site performance or isolated rendering cost.')
s=s.replace('Production eligibility and instruction savings require separate\nverification.', 'Production diagnostics verify eligibility; the matched combined-policy\ncomparison and its limits are recorded in the report above.')
p.write_text(s)
p=Path('OPTIMIZED_SITES.md');s=p.read_text();anchor='## Historical result awaiting raw verification\n';assert anchor in s
addition=f'''## GitHub full-JavaScript site-policy comparison

The GitHub site policies reduce observed instructions by **{median:.2f}% between
medians** and **{conservative:.2f}% conservatively** across seven matched pairs on
`github.com/vlang/v`. Control median: **{v['median_control']:,}**; optimized median:
**{v['median_candidate']:,}**. This is a Vox policy-on/policy-off comparison on the
same completed build `91be2b76`, with full immediate JavaScriptCore startup,
original-origin frozen replay, a shared Date prefix, fresh profiles/caches and
five-second settling after Sponsor/sidebar readiness. The launch-through-document
PNG/audit/teardown scope uses 1024×768 at 1×; all fourteen PNGs match the unchanged
reference exactly and complete content audits pass. Counts are process-tree lower
bounds and exclude GPU/WindowServer work. Live loading passes separately; live
performance, isolated rendering, scrolling and comparison with Brave are outside
this result. [Report and limitations](docs/GITHUB_SITE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md),
[exact counts and retained attempts](docs/performance/github-raster-input-validation-20261108.json).

'''
s=s.replace(anchor,addition+anchor,1);p.write_text(s)
print(f'Median reduction {median:.6f}%, conservative {conservative:.6f}%')

vlang.io

Key Features of V

Simplicity: the language can be learned over the course of a weekend
Fast compilation: ≈110k loc/s with a Clang backend,
≈500k loc/s with native and tcc backends (Intel i5-7500, SSD, no
optimization) (demo video)
Easy to develop: V compiles itself in less than a second
Performance: as fast as C (V's main backend compiles to human-readable C)
Safety: no null, no globals, no undefined behavior (wip), immutability by default
C to V translation (Translating DOOM demo video)
Hot code reloading
Flexible memory management. GC by default, manual via v -gc none,
arena allocation via v -prealloc, autofree via v -autofree
(autofree demo video).
Cross-platform UI library
Built-in graphics library
Easy cross-compilation
REPL
Built-in ORM
Built-in web framework
C and JavaScript backends
Great for writing low-level software (Vinix OS)

Stability, future changes, post 1.0 freeze
Despite being at an early development stage, the V language is relatively stable, and doesn't
change often. But there will be changes before 1.0.
Most changes in the syntax are handled via vfmt automatically.
The V core APIs (primarily the os module) will also have minor changes until
they are stabilized in V 1.0. Of course, the APIs will grow after that, but without breaking
existing code.
After the 1.0 release V is going to be in the "feature freeze" mode. That means no breaking changes
in the language, only bug fixes and performance improvements. Similar to Go.
Will there be V 2.0? Not within a decade after 1.0, perhaps not ever.
To sum it up, unlike many other languages, V is not going to be always changing, with new features
introduced and old features modified. It is always going to be a small and simple
language, very similar to the way it is right now.
Installing V from source
This is the preferred method.
Linux, macOS, Windows, *BSD, Solaris, WSL, etc.
Usually, installing V is quite simple if you have an environment that already has a
functional git installation.
Note: On Windows, run makev.bat instead of make in CMD, or ./makev.bat in
PowerShell.
To build with Visual Studio, run makev.bat -msvc. If the bundled TCC bootstrap cannot be
compiled or fails while building the next compiler stage, the script retries with MSVC,
then Clang and GCC.
Windows ARM64 releases are available as v_windows_arm64.zip. Install Visual Studio's
C++ ARM64 build tools and a Windows SDK, then use v -cc msvc file.v to build native
applications with the C backend. To build the compiler and release tools from source,
run ./cmd/tools/builders/windows_arm64_release.ps1 in native ARM64 PowerShell 7 on Windows 11.
Source bootstrapping also needs Visual Studio's x64 C++ tools and Windows 11's x64 emulation
to run the downloaded Windows snapshot. The script then explicitly targets ARM64 for the
compiler stages, release tools, and application smoke test, checking their PE architecture.
It builds and runs an application before packaging and does not require an x64 TCC bundle.
On native Windows ARM64, v up -skip_v_self uses this same bootstrap script and requires
native ARM64 PowerShell 7 and both Visual Studio toolchains; it keeps the compiler native.
makev.bat -clang keeps Clang's installed target: LLVM-MinGW uses its GNU runtime,
while Visual Studio's Clang uses the adjacent clang-cl.exe and the MSVC SDK.
Note: On FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly, and Solaris, install GNU make and run it as
gmake.
Note: On Ubuntu/Debian, you may need to run sudo apt install git build-essential make first.
To get started, execute the following in your terminal/shell:
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/vlang/v
cd v
make
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
That should be it, and you should find your V executable at [path to V repo]/v.
[path to V repo] can be anywhere.
On Unix-like systems, make and the v self bootstrap fallback stream compatibility fixes
for older vc/v.c snapshots to the C compiler. These match the peak RSS helper's return type
to i64, guard Linux-only prctl code, and teach pre-uint compilers the new integer
spelling and allocator signatures. The snapshot stays unchanged on disk.
The compatibility filter uses the system sh; Bash is not required.
On Windows, builds use PowerShell to prepare a temporary snapshot with the same integer
compatibility fixes. makev.bat generates the first compiler stage as C and links it directly.
This also works with older bootstrap snapshots whose process-spawn code is broken.
Direct TCC links add the installed bundle's thirdparty\tcc\lib\openlibm.o, when present,
for C99 math functions such as remainder. Each bundle ships this object for its own compiler,
so an existing amd64 or i386 checkout links a matching object even when it differs from the
branch selected by the host, -tcc32, or TCC_BRANCH.
For paths longer than 260 characters, see Long paths on Windows.
(Like the note above says, on Windows, use makev.bat, instead of make.)
Now try running ./v run examples/hello_world.v (or v run examples/hello_world.v in cmd shell).

Trouble? Please see the notes above, and link to
Installation Issues
for help.

Note: V is being constantly updated. To update V to its latest version, simply run:
v up
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
This also refreshes the bundled TCC binaries used for fast C compilation.
It then runs v wipe-cache to clear module, object, temporary, and compiled tool caches,
even when V is already up to date. Subsequent builds recreate the caches they need;
v up does not replay previously recorded build configurations or test selectors.
NoteIf you run into any trouble, or you have a different operating
system or Linux distribution that doesn't install or work immediately, please see
Installation Issues
and search for your OS and problem.
If you can't find your problem, please add it to an existing discussion if one exists for
your OS, or create a new one if a main discussion doesn't yet exist for your OS.

C compiler
The Tiny C Compiler (tcc) is downloaded for you by make if
there is a compatible version for your system, and installed under the V thirdparty directory.
For regular non-production builds on supported hosts, V prefers a working bundled TCC, then a
working tcc from PATH, before using the platform compiler. The system fallback is selected only
when required V runtime artifacts are available, including the bundled libgc.a used by default
glibc and Windows Boehm builds.
On macOS, regular builds and v self use TCC by default, including on Darwin 27 and later.
Use a current TCC bundle built with the Mach-O zero-fill fix for
#29744; older bundles can corrupt global variables.
An explicit -cc overrides the default, and CC also overrides the compiler used by v self.
-prod builds never default to TCC, which cannot do their optimizations. On x64 Windows,
without -cc, a -prod build uses MSVC when an x64 Visual Studio Developer environment is
active (cl on PATH, with INCLUDE and LIB set; not for -o file.o), otherwise a clang
that targets x86_64 MinGW, otherwise gcc. A native -prod build on another Windows
architecture uses gcc. An explicit -cc always wins.
An explicit -cc msvc on Windows does not need a Developer environment. When INCLUDE or LIB
is not set, V finds the Visual Studio C++ tools (the cl on PATH, VCToolsInstallDir, or the
newest installation vswhere reports) and the Windows SDK (WindowsSdkDir, the KitsRoot10
registry value, or Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10). Expandable registry values use the
current environment. V puts a cl for the architecture V
builds for on PATH when none is there, or when the one there is for another architecture (unless
-cc names it by its path), and sets the missing variables for the C compiler. Variables that are
already set, as in a Developer Command Prompt, are left as they are. The program that v run
starts gets the environment it was started with, not these changes. If V cannot find tools for
the requested architecture or a usable SDK, it reports what is missing before cl fails.
On macOS, -cc tcc -gc boehm uses a persistent bundled libgc.dylib store when the physical V
installation path contains a comma. The store is under $XDG_DATA_HOME/v-tcc-libgc-v1, or
$HOME/.local/share/v-tcc-libgc-v1 when the XDG variable is unset or empty. V creates the fallback
directories with private permissions. An explicit XDG_DATA_HOME must already be absolute,
user-owned, not group/world-writable, and have a safe, comma-free canonical path. Compiled binaries
can depend on this store at runtime, so do not delete it while they are in use.
This compiler is very fast, but does almost no optimizations. It is best for development builds.
For production builds (using the -prod option to V), it's recommended to use clang, gcc, or
Microsoft Visual C++. If you are doing development, you most likely already have one of those
installed.
Otherwise, follow these instructions:

Symlinking
NoteIt is highly recommended, that you put V on your PATH. That saves
you the effort to type in the full path to your v executable every time.
V provides a convenience v symlink command to do that more easily.

On Unix systems, it creates a v symlink in /usr/local/bin by
default. To do that, run:
sudo ./v symlink
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
You can also pass a different directory, for example:
./v symlink ~/.local/bin
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
On Windows, start a new shell with administrative privileges, for example by pressing the
Windows Key, then type cmd.exe, right-click on its menu entry, and choose Run as administrator. In the new administrative shell, cd to the path where you have compiled V, then
type:
v symlink
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
(or .\v symlink in PowerShell)
You can pass a different directory there too, for example
v symlink C:\Users\you\bin.
That will make V available everywhere, by adding it to your PATH. Please restart your
shell/editor after that, so that it can pick up the new PATH variable.
NoteThere is no need to run v symlink more than once - v will still be available, even after
v up, restarts, and so on. You only need to run it again if you decide to move the V repo
folder somewhere else.

Testing and running the examples
Make sure V can compile itself:
$ v self

V 0.3.x
Use Ctrl-C or `exit` to exit

>>> println('hello world')
hello world
>>>
    
      
    

      
    

    
  
v self defaults to -gc none and includes only the C backend. Selecting an omitted backend
automatically builds and runs a cached full compiler. Later requests reuse it while its sources
are current. Use v -all-backends self or v -compile-backend fastc self to include optional
backends in the main executable. Pass -gc <mode> if you need a different GC mode.
On non-Windows hosts, v -prod self uses profile-guided optimization (PGO) when the selected C
compiler is Clang and llvm-profdata is available. Clang's reported installation directory and
resolved executable directory are searched before PATH and macOS xcrun for the profile tool,
keeping LLVM versions together.
Both -cc clang and -cc=clang select that toolchain; the last compiler option takes precedence.
It builds an instrumented compiler, trains it on
uncached self-compilation, then builds the optimized compiler. This takes longer to build the
production compiler. Other C toolchains and failed PGO attempts use a regular production build.
Use v -prod -parallel-cc self to skip PGO and compile the generated C units in parallel.
Explicit -no-prod-options or profile-related -cflags also skip automatic PGO.
Use v -b arm64 file.v on macOS ARM64 or v -b x64 file.v on Linux AMD64 to compile
with a native backend. Use v -b arm64 self or v -b x64 self to rebuild
the full compiler with the selected native backend. A backend-specific self x2 replaces
the compiler twice, so the second build runs the compiler produced by the first native
build. Use -o v_arm64 or -o v_x64 to keep the current compiler and write a separate
executable. Native self-builds use -gc none and retain commands such as self, fmt,
and version. The native compiler includes the C backend and leaves out FastC by default.
For x64, add -prod to enable SSA optimization, register allocation and optimized C helpers.
Very large x64 modules may skip the global SSA pass to bound compiler memory. The ARM64
backend retains its existing optimization behavior.

V net.http, net.websocket, v install
The net.http module, the net.websocket module, and the v install command may all use SSL.
V comes with a version of mbedtls, which should work on all systems. If you find a need to
use OpenSSL instead, you will need to make sure that it is installed on your system, then
use the -d use_openssl switch when you compile.
Note: Mbed-TLS is smaller and easier to install on windows too (V comes with it), but if you
write programs, that do lots of http requests to HTTPS/SSL servers, in most cases, it is best
to compile with -d use_openssl, and do so on a system, where you do have OpenSSL installed
(see below). Mbed-TLS is slower, and can have more issues, especially when you are doing parallel
http requests to multiple hosts (for example in web scrapers, REST API clients, RSS readers, etc).
On windows, it is better to run such programs in WSL2.
